claims: Men aged 18 through 25 in the United States are required to register with the Selective Service System (SSS) for a potential military draft.
A military draft is not currently active.
Registration with the Selective Service System is mandatory for male citizens and immigrants aged 18-25.
Men must register with the Selective Service System within 30 days of turning 18.
Selective Service System registration is required up until age 26.
Male U.S. citizens residing in the US must register with the Selective Service System.
Male immigrants including residents, refugees, and undocumented residing in the US must register with the Selective Service System.
A 2026 federal law further ensures automatic registration of eligible men.
People on active duty in the armed forces are exempt from Selective Service System registration while on duty.
People in the military academies are exempt from Selective Service System registration while on duty.
High school students can have their induction postponed until graduation or until they turn 20.
College students can have their induction postponed until the end of the semester.
College seniors can have their induction postponed until the end of the academic year.
Failure to register with the Selective Service System is a felony.
Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include up to five years in prison.
Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include up to $250,000 in fines.
Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include loss of eligibility for federal student loans.
Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include loss of eligibility for training.
Penalties for failure to register with the Selective Service System include loss of eligibility for citizenship
